entries.title: revert the lagging platform pins that blocked 0.27.0 and 0.27.1
entries.body:
* fix(cli): let a release follow one that never published

0.27.0 failed before it published, so its lockfile job never moved the
platform pins, and 0.27.1 came up pinning 0.26.0. The pin-age check in
tests/run.js allowed only this version or the one before, so 0.27.1 went
red as well, and every later release would have too. The check now also
allows the seed's version: the last release that reached its GitHub
release.

The release workflow also gets more resilient. Each npm publish is tried
three times, and a failed try that still left the version on the registry
counts as done (0.26.0's first attempt died on a Sigstore 409). The
lockfile job now waits up to 15 minutes for the registry, not 5 (0.25.0
ran past the old limit).

Tests: node tests/run.js package (261 passed), release (47), pin-platform (21)

* Revert "fix(cli): let a release follow one that never published"

This reverts commit a523e43d9d7ff18afd7b334c22def823c29bf956.

* Revert "fix(cli): install the main package with its pins stamped, as release.yml publishes it (#1070)"

This reverts commit 9ed9675e3a76f3344654825230f533085fcf2670.

* Revert "ci: keep main's platform pins one release behind so every commit agrees with its lockfile (#1039)"

This reverts commit 5db6f0b1245684a9c82647256b1d3775b1adb89f.

* build: pin the platform packages to 0.27.1, as the restored release bump does

With the lagging-pins flow reverted, the release commit moves the
optionalDependencies pins with the version again, and tests/run.js wants
them equal to it. 0.27.1's release commit was cut under the reverted flow
and left them at 0.26.0, so this moves them by hand, in package.json and
the lockfile root, the way release-pr.yml now would have.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon
